slot.brief: A person standing on a lift accelerating upward/downward; ask the apparent weight as a multiple of true weight using N = m(g ± a).

stem: A person stands on a weighing scale inside an elevator that is accelerating downwards with an acceleration of $0.2g$. The ratio of the apparent weight to the true weight of the person is:

verdicts.working: Apparent weight N = m(g − a) = m(g − 0.2g) = 0.8mg. Ratio N/(mg) = 0.8.

working:
The true weight of the person is $W = mg$.
When the elevator accelerates downwards with an acceleration $a$, the normal reaction force (apparent weight $W'$) exerted on the person by the weighing scale is given by:
$$mg - N = ma \implies N = m(g - a)$$
Given $a = 0.2g$:
$$W' = N = m(g - 0.2g) = 0.8mg$$
The ratio of the apparent weight to the true weight is:
$$\dfrac{W'}{W} = \dfrac{0.8mg}{mg} = 0.8$$

Independent check: Apparent weight N = m(g − a) = m(g − 0.2g) = 0.8mg. Ratio N/(mg) = 0.8.

draft.distractor_notes:

- $1.0$: Neglects the acceleration of the elevator, assuming apparent weight equals true weight.
